pages.name: What this system is, and is not

text.content:
This is an unofficial Foundry VTT system for Mongoose Traveller, second edition. It runs on Foundry v14. Traveller is the property of Mongoose Publishing, which neither made nor endorsed it, and you still need the books.

It is meant to run a campaign rather than hold a character sheet: group creation, the damage chain, personal and space combat, trade, jump travel and a ship's accounts. Each of those is a screen or a sheet you can operate, and each cites the book and page it implements.

These are the kinds of Actor it knows:

TypeSub-types
TravellerNone
NPCPerson · Creature
RobotNone
SpacecraftNone
StashNone
VehicleNone
WorldNone

What it does not contain

No rules text, and no printed content. The system ships procedures and the numbers those procedures need. A blank world has no careers, no species, no weapons and no ships, because those are Mongoose's to distribute. You type in what you use, or bring it from your own library.

What does ship is five compendiums, grouped in the MGT2 folder.

PackAnswers
MGT2 — Guide to the systemHow do I operate this? You are reading it.
MGT2 — What this system does with the rulesDoes this screen follow the book, and what does it leave to me?
MGT2 — Demo actors, annotatedWhat does a correctly filled Actor look like?
MGT2 — Demo items, annotatedWhat does a correctly filled Item look like?
MGT2 — Demo scenes, annotatedWhat does a Region with a hazard on it look like?

Everything in the three demo packs is invented: a harbour world, its patrol, its careers and a courier that appear in no book. They are enough to run every step of this first part, and @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.NcoUzlc1COPloUV3]{Configuring your own content} explains what each document teaches.

What the books are still for

  • What things mean. A sheet prints a skill, a trait or a difficulty rung. The book says what it means in play.
  • When a rule applies. The system works out what a check is worth. Calling for it, choosing its difficulty and ruling on the result stay with the referee.
  • The content. A career's tables, a species' frame and a ship's statblock come from your copy of the book.
  • Whatever has no number under it. Where a printed rule gives nothing to compute, the card states it and stops. See @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.ZPr9rPt1v4Xq0HqD]{What this system deliberately does not do}.

Three habits of the system

It computes, and you decide. A ship's sheet works out its mortgage and collects nothing. A card works out a wound and writes nothing until somebody presses Apply.

Nothing runs on a clock. The system has no tick and no advance time control. The one date it keeps is a number you type, and even a combat round moves only when you move it.

Every modifier has a name. The roll prompt lists what stands on a check, one source to a row, and a row can be unticked for this one roll. If a total surprises you, the terms are there to read.

How to read this guide

Part 1 is these six pages. Read them once, in order, with a new world open. Each one gives real steps in the order a referee takes them and ends by pointing at the reference page for that subject.

  • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.6YnPpN3Zc0K7Po2G]{Setting up a world}: the packs, the optional rules, the shared tables, the campaign day.
  • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.Qxd9kRrnKDKjT0SG]{A first Traveller}: creation, one term at a time, and the sheet it leaves behind.
  • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.NunxFrsIdM3SVCrT]{A first check}: the roll prompt, the card, and a second check chained from the first.
  • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.VASOi4kPsoKQAAHJ]{A first fight}: initiative, an attack, the damage chain and a Reaction.
  • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.YVNlkmJlADkz5azu]{A first ship}: a hull, its crew and mounts, then a jump.

Part 2, from @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.32DXnPgHrfV65dkn]{The character sheet} on, is for consulting. A ? in the title bar of a sheet opens the guide at that sheet's page, and so does the one on the creation, voyage, space combat and Docket windows and on the roll prompt.

This page leaves you with a world ready for the rest of the walkthrough. Four things are the referee's before anyone sits down: the packs your library will live in, the optional rules, the tables every career shares, and the date.

Create the world

In Foundry's Setup screen, create a world on this system and launch it as the Gamemaster. No module is needed.

Open the Compendium tab. The MGT2 folder holds the five packs that @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.DlXbzmjppzqEqVRm]{What this system is, and is not} described. Leave them where they are. A demo document works in several places straight from its pack, and the steps below say when to import one. Importing is Foundry's own: drag the entry to the sidebar, or right-click it and choose Import.

Create the world's packs

A compendium is where your transcribed content will outlive any one world. The system can make the shelves for you.

  1. Open Configure Settings and find this system's settings.
  2. Press Create packs, beside World compendium packs.
  3. Read the five rows, and press Create.
RowHoldsSeen byTicked
LibraryItemsplayersyes
Ships & VehiclesActorsplayersyes
NPCs & CreaturesActorsreferee onlyyes
TablesRoll tablesreferee onlyno
Notes & HandoutsJournalsreferee onlyno

The last two start unticked because a referee who wants neither should not have to delete them afterwards.

The packs arrive empty and unlocked in a Traveller folder. The referee-only rows are closed as they are created, because Foundry leaves a new pack readable by every player. You can press the button again later: a row that exists is greyed out, only what is missing is made, and nothing is ever deleted or overwritten.

Creation's shared tables are not Foundry roll tables. They are career Items, so your own go in the Library. The Tables pack is for your own random tables, and no screen reads it.

Read the optional rules

Press Configure rules, beside Optional and variant rules. The window has a page per domain, and only the referee can open it.

For a first session, change nothing. Every default is the reading the books best support, and the rest of this walkthrough assumes the defaults. Read these before you move on, because they shape what you will see:

  • Character creation is the page to settle before anyone rolls. How rolled numbers reach characteristics starts on assigning in any order, and Iron Man, boon dice and a cap on terms all start off.
  • Psionics, on the Travellers page, starts off. With it off, no PSI appears anywhere.
  • Encumbrance and Count rounds against the magazine start on, so a carried load and a fired round both do something.
  • Jump procedure for new ships starts on the Core procedure.

A change is written as you make it and every open sheet redraws, so you can come back to this window in the middle of a session. @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.Ca06CCZpxbTWBWGG]{Optional rules} has every rule and its default.

Link the shared tables

Some tables belong to no career: Life Events, the Draft and the like. The system ships none, and a table nobody links is replaced by a sentence asking you to roll it yourself. The demo packs hold a set, which is what @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.Qxd9kRrnKDKjT0SG]{A first Traveller} will use.

  1. Press Link tables, beside Shared creation tables.
  2. Open MGT2 — Demo items, annotated beside it.
  3. Drag each of these onto its row:
    • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoTableLifeEvt]{Demo — Harbour Life Events} on Life Events
    • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoTableUnusual]{Demo — Harbour Unusual Events} on Unusual Event
    • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoTableDraftBw]{Demo — Bellweather Draft} on Draft
    • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoTableBackSkl]{Demo — Bellweather Background Skills} on Background Skills
  4. Leave Pre-Career Events empty. Both demo schools print their own events, so linking it would change nothing for them.
  5. Press Save.

The tables may stay in the pack. One document does need importing: @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoCareerQuayHd]{Demo — Quay Hands}. A Traveller who is refused a career may turn to a career that is always open, and that list skips both demo packs, so import this one into the world to put it on the list.

Set the campaign day

The Campaign day setting, in the same pane, is the only date the system keeps. It is a whole number, counted from whatever day you call zero. It starts at 0, and nothing advances it but you: not a jump, not a rest, not a voyage.

Type 200 for this walkthrough, and press Save Changes. The demo ship and its cargo are stamped around that day, so 200 puts them in their own present. Speculative trade reads the campaign day for a supplier's month, freight for its deadline and a ship for the service it owes. A table that never touches it will see all three stand still.

What you have now

Five empty shelves at most, the default rules, four linked tables, one career in the world, and a date. The other settings in the pane are described on @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.L1PCQIr60xQbIsD1]{Settings}. The palette among them is per person, so each player can repaint their own screen.

Next: @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.Qxd9kRrnKDKjT0SG]{A first Traveller}.

Traveller creation is played rather than filled in. This page takes one Traveller through one career with the demo documents, then looks at what it left on the sheet. It assumes the tables from @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.6YnPpN3Zc0K7Po2G]{Setting up a world} are linked. @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.XAy8tHQw02RmRtPC]{Character creation} is the full reference.

The same screen runs on careers and species you supply yourself, and nothing below changes but the names.

Make a blank Traveller

  1. In the Actors tab, create an Actor of type Traveller.
  2. If a player will run it, give them ownership with Foundry's own Ownership window. Only someone who can edit a Traveller can run their steps, so the owner rolls.
  3. The sheet opens with Character creation not started. Press Start.

The creation window opens with one column for this Traveller. A table creates together (Core p.8): each player presses Start on their own, or drags their Traveller to the foot of the grid, and each gets a column. Clicking a column selects it, and the strip below the grid then shows that Traveller's term.

You can stop at any moment. Everything decided is already on the Traveller, and the Character creation button at the head of the Actors tab reopens the window on the same roster.

Leave the species empty

A species is one Item on the Traveller, and for creation it is a frame: what is rolled, how old they start, how long a term lasts and which steps a term runs. With none, the strip names the frame default, which is the Core sequence on six characteristics. That is what the rest of this page uses.

On a second Traveller, drop @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoSpeciesSopho]{Demo — Sophont} on their column before rolling anything. The strip gains a step of the species' own, and what is rolled changes with it. The sheet stores a pointer to the Item and copies nothing, so a species' modifiers stand beside the rolled scores and go when it goes.

Characteristics and background

Two chips stand before the numbered steps, because they run once and not once a term. Take them left to right.

  1. Press Characteristics. The dice post to chat in one card, and a dialog offers the results. Each picker holds a distinct result, and changing one swaps the two. Press Assign, and the chip shows the UPP.
  2. Press Background skills. The allowance is EDU DM + 3 (Core p.9). Each row suggests the skills of the linked table, and you may type another. Press Take them. The skills arrive at level 0.

Choose a career

Open MGT2 — Demo items, annotated and drag @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoCareerHarbor]{Demo — Harbour Patrol} onto the Traveller's sheet. The grid refuses a career and says where it belongs. The drop copies the whole career onto the Traveller as a record, and that record is what the term writes to.

One term

The strip is the term's only control. Press the highlighted step, read what happens, and press the next. Most steps roll at once and post a card, and a dialog appears only where there is something to choose.

  1. Start-of-term elections asks about anagathics (Core p.49). Answer no.
  2. Qualification rolls the career's own line, END 6+ here. A pass enters the career and pays rank 0 at once, which on this ladder is Seafarer 1.
  3. Basic training gives every skill on the Service Skills table at level 0. In a first career that takes the place of the term's skill roll (Core p.18).
  4. Skill roll spends what the counter on the tray holds. Pick a table and it rolls 1D. It comes before Survival (Core p.18). In this first term basic training has taken its place, so the counter is empty and the cursor passes over it.
  5. Survival rolls END 6+. A natural 2 always fails, and a failure rolls on the career's Mishaps.
  6. Event rolls 2D on the career's Events. A row may ask a question or throw a check of its own, and a 7 goes to the linked Life Events.
  7. Commission does nothing here, because the Patrol prints none. Press it and move on.
  8. Advancement rolls INT 7+. A pass is the next rank, its bonus and an extra skill roll (Core p.18). The cursor goes back to Skill roll to spend it.
  9. Ageing says none is due. It starts with the fourth term.
  10. Continue or leave closes the term. Press Leave the career for this first run, or Continue to go round again.

Closing the term logs its years, credits its Benefit roll and moves the column on. A second term of the same career skips Qualification's roll and repeats the rest, so a longer life is only more presses.

If Qualification fails, the career comes off the sheet and a dialog offers the draft, a career always open, or deciding later. The term is not lost. The draft rolls the table you linked and enters its career with no roll, and the always-open list finds your imported Quay Hands. @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.XAy8tHQw02RmRtPC]{Character creation} covers the rest of what can go wrong, which is a fair part of the game.

If ageing takes a score to 0, that is a crisis, and from then on every qualification fails, a change of assignment included. PSI is the exception: aged to 0 it is no crisis, but every psionic ability is gone for good, so talents refuse to roll and a psionic career stays shut.

Steps can be pressed out of order, because the sequence is the table's discipline rather than a lock. Each runs once a term, except the skill roll. If one must run again, the referee reopens it with the arrow beside it on the strip.

Muster out

When a Traveller leaves their last career, the masthead's Muster out button opens the closing screen. It lists each Traveller's service, the Benefit rolls they are owed and what they have taken.

  1. Press Roll a Benefit, choose the career and a column, and confirm. Cash goes to the Traveller's purse, and a skill, a score or a contact applies at once.
  2. Repeat until the rolls are spent. A row that names a piece of kit, such as @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoArmorDeckVst]{Demo — Deck Vest}, is written down as a right rather than an object. Drag the Item from the pack to the sheet yourself.
  3. Press Finish on the Traveller's row, and confirm. The dialog lists anything you would be walking away from.

Finishing banks the pension, pays any debt out of the Traveller's Cash, writes the Traveller's age on the sheet and removes the creation ledger. An age you typed yourself stays. An age the system wrote is kept current. The column goes, and the strip on the sheet goes with it. The cross on a column is not the same thing: it takes a Traveller off the roster with no banking and no payment.

Read the sheet

Open the finished Traveller. The sheet is in Play, and it always opens there.

  • Characteristics. Each score keeps its rolled value as base, and nothing should ever rewrite it. Anything that moves a score later is a row of its own, in Permanent changes on the Health tab.
  • Skills. On the Traits & Skills tab. A skill is a talent Item embedded on the Traveller, and everything that reads a skill matches it by name. There is no list of skills on the Actor, which is why a blank Traveller has none. A speciality makes a skill of its own, so a bare Gun Combat grant does not raise a held Gun Combat (slug). Click a skill's name to roll it.
  • Careers. One row for the record, with its terms and rank.
  • Money and gear. Cash On Hand and the Benefits ledger are on the Inventory tab, under Finance.

Play and Edit. The Play / Edit button in the title bar switches the mode for this open window only. Edit is for structure: the base scores, the name, the + on Skills and Careers, every gear icon. Press it and those controls appear. Press it again to go back. Everything that changes during a session, such as a wound, a roll or equipping a vest, stays live in Play, so a referee rarely leaves it in the middle of a game.

The other road

Creation is optional, and the sheet does not depend on it. For a Traveller finished on paper, press Edit, type the six base scores, and add skills with the + or by dropping one. @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoSkillGunSlug]{Gun Combat (slug)} is a skill to drop: open it and set the level, because a skill in a compendium is a template and the level belongs to whoever holds it. A career Item dropped on the sheet makes a record in the same way. The not started strip goes as soon as a score or a skill is written.

Five finished Travellers

Each of these is the output of a real run of this screen, so each shows what a particular road leaves behind. Open them beside your own.

  • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-actors.Actor.demoCharTamsinRv]{Demo — Tamsin Reeve} took a cadet school with honours and served one career to a voluntary exit.
  • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-actors.Actor.demoCharCorvinDr]{Demo — Corvin Dray} was refused and drafted, and paid a surgeon.
  • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-actors.Actor.demoCharHesperLd]{Demo — Hesper Lund} ran on to an ageing crisis and a pension.
  • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-actors.Actor.demoCharJorenPsk]{Demo — Joren Pask} changed assignment and career, and made a contact, a rival and an ally.
  • @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-actors.Actor.demoCharMirelAst]{Demo — Mirel Aston} is unfinished. Import her and she stands on your roster in the middle of a term, which is the quickest way to see one in progress.

@UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.32DXnPgHrfV65dkn]{The character sheet} covers every block. Next: @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.NunxFrsIdM3SVCrT]{A first check}.

Nearly every roll in the system goes through one window, so this is the page to take slowly. Import @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-actors.Actor.demoCharTravellr]{Demo — Traveller} and open her sheet. Her gear puts a standing modifier on the prompt, which a Traveller fresh from creation does not have. @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.AFpVHfj7ijV7S9ct]{The roll prompt in full} has every row.

Open the prompt

On the Traits & Skills tab, click Investigate. The roll prompt opens. Nothing is spent and nothing is written while it is open, so you can try everything below and still close it.

The window builds itself from what is being rolled. This one is short, because a skill check needs little. A weapon's is long, as the next page shows.

Where each DM comes from

Check holds the characteristic and the skill. Her INT and her Investigate level are each a term, and the small figure beside each select is what it adds. The skill select opens with two entries that look alike and are not: No skill — characteristic check is DM+0, because no skill is missing, and Not proficient is the DM-3 of a skill she lacks (Core p.58-59).

Modifiers lists whatever stands on her at this moment, one source to a row, already ticked. Here that is Actor modifier: @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoTrinketFob01]{Demo — Lucky Fob} carries an Active Effect that adds to every check. A row for @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoAugmentRefl1]{Demo — Reflex Wiring} stands below it unticked, because that augment boosts Gun Combat and this check is Investigate. Untick the Actor modifier row and the total falls, for this roll only. That is what waivable means in this system, and the sheet is not changed. Fatigue, encumbrance or armour worn without its skill would each be a row here too.

Custom DM takes any number you rule. Timeframes is the DM for taking longer or rushing (Core p.63).

The live formula and the Effect

The foot of the window is live. It shows the dice and the total DM, the target and every term by name, and all of it follows what you do above.

Under that is a strip of Effect, from failure to success, with a marker on where the check lands. The marker assumes a roll of 7, the average of 2D, and the caption says so. Effect is the total less the target (Core p.61), and much of this system runs on it, so a player choosing between two options can see the Effect before the dice.

  1. On the Target ladder, press 10+. The name Difficult appears beside it and the marker slides towards failure.
  2. Press 6+. It slides back.
  3. Press the empty cell. No difficulty is stated, so the check is measured against Average 8+ (Core p.61), and the card will say that was assumed.

Choose a rung and leave it there.

Boon, Roll and Bane

The three buttons at the foot are also the choice of dice: Bane rolls 3D and keeps the two lowest, Roll rolls 2D, and Boon rolls 3D and keeps the two highest (Core p.61). They do not stack, so a check has one, the other or neither.

Press Roll.

Read the card

The card names the check and what it was measured against. Under that is the dice line. Click it to open the dice and every named term, which is where anyone at the table can audit the roll.

Then comes the Effect, with its band and a colour to match. The band names are the book's, and @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.Fi5TR1jZrgXracji]{Chat cards} lists them.

A check card writes nothing to any sheet. Whatever follows is a button, or your ruling.

Chain a second check

Tasks often run in sequence, and the Effect of one becomes a DM on the next (Core p.63). Say she has found the discrepancy and now has to talk her way past the clerk.

  1. Click Persuade. The prompt now has two more rows, because the log holds a check with an Effect.
  2. In Chain, select the Investigate card. The DM appears beside it and joins the formula as a named term.
  3. Press Roll.

The DM is read off the book's table and is never the raw Effect, so a narrow failure still costs something and a marginal success still helps. Selecting several cards is how working together is done: one table, read once per contributor. A check already used is marked, and still allowed.

The new card opens with a strip naming its source, and that link scrolls the log back to it, so a chain can be followed afterwards.

Opposed, the row beneath Chain, changes no number. The check rolls as normal and its card compares the two Effects (Core p.62).

If your table chains often, the world setting Check cards: Chain into button adds a one-click offer to every card that has an Effect. It starts off.

When the referee asks

So far the player chose to roll. Usually the referee calls for the check, and for that there is @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.TUwYdm40vTQJiuSJ]{the Docket}, the clipboard control beside the chat input. You compose one demand, see what it costs each Traveller before it is sent, and post a single card the table answers on. The prompt then opens with what you fixed marked GM, and the player can no longer change it.

Next: @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.VASOi4kPsoKQAAHJ]{A first fight}.

Personal combat runs on Foundry's own combat tracker, with no separate screen. A fight is the checks of @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.NunxFrsIdM3SVCrT]{A first check}, plus four things: an initiative order, an attack, a wound and a Reaction. This page sets @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-actors.Actor.demoCharTravellr]{Demo — Traveller} against a @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-actors.Actor.demoNpcMarshRunr]{Demo — Marsh Runner}. Import both.

Place the fighters

  1. Create a scene with Foundry's defaults, and activate it.
  2. Drag the Traveller and the Marsh Runner onto it.
  3. Select both tokens, right-click one, and use Toggle Combat State on the token's HUD.

The Traveller's token is linked to her Actor. The creature's is not, so each one you drop takes its own damage, and you open its sheet by double-clicking the token. The Combat tab now holds an encounter.

Sides and surprise

Right-click a combatant in the tracker and choose Side and Initiative. This menu, and the Reactions below, are the referee's.

  • Side was guessed from the token's disposition. Correct it if the guess is wrong.
  • Ambush is DM+6 or DM-6 on Initiative (Core p.73).
  • Tactics Effect takes the Effect of a Tactics check, which reaches everyone on that side (Core p.73). A surprised combatant cannot hold it.

All three feed the Initiative roll, so settle them first. A fight with no surprise needs nothing here but the sides.

Initiative is an Effect

Core p.73 makes Initiative the Effect of a DEX or INT check, and the system takes that literally.

  1. Press the die on the Marsh Runner's row. It rolls 2D plus its DM against 8, and writes the Effect.
  2. For the Traveller, click the word Initiative on her sheet. That opens the roll prompt, where a player may take INT in place of DEX. Leave the Target empty and press Roll. The Effect goes to her combatant as the card posts.
  3. Press Begin Combat.

So the numbers in the tracker are small, and they can be negative. A 0 is an ordinary result. The tracker's die also works for a Traveller, and it reads the characteristic set in their Configuration. It adds hundredths, the DEX tiebreak, which are no part of the Effect. A roll from the sheet writes the bare Effect.

Ask for Initiative, in the tracker's menu, opens the Docket on the whole encounter. Its answers land on the request card and do not reach the tracker, so type each Effect into the tracker's own field.

The attack

  1. Hover over the creature's token and press T to target it.
  2. On the Traveller's sheet, open the Inventory tab and click Demo — Sidearm under On Hand. The prompt opens as an attack, on DEX and the weapon's Average 8+.
  3. Read the skill select. It opens on her Gun Combat (slug), because the weapon on her sheet is bound to that skill by id. A binding belongs to one Actor, so the same weapon dropped from the pack on another sheet opens on Not proficient until you pick the skill on the weapon's own sheet.
  4. Read the Range row. With one token targeted, the Distance arrives filled from the canvas and the band paints itself beside it with its DM. Type over it if you prefer.
  5. The creature's sheet prints a Size DM for its attacker, and no prompt reads it. Add it with Custom DM.
  6. Read the Traits chips. The pistol is loaded with @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoAmmoMagnum01]{Demo — Magnum Rounds}, whose traits replace the pistol's, so the chip says Lo-Pen. It is dashed because it does nothing to this roll. It travels with the attack to the damage card.
  7. Press Roll.

The round comes out of the magazine as the check rolls, and the card says so. A magazine that cannot pay refuses the shot.

The card now carries Roll damage, naming the Effect it will add (Core p.77). Press it. It posts the damage card. A miss carries no Roll damage: damage is rolled on a successful attack (Core p.74). A weapon with Blast is the exception, because its miss may still catch someone nearby (Core p.131), so it keeps the button and rolls with no Effect added.

Apply the damage

Attackers do not resolve damage. The defender does. The damage card names no target on purpose.

  1. Select the creature's token. A target is not enough: Apply reads the tokens you have selected.
  2. Press Apply on the damage card.

Here the creature's Armour trait gives it Protection, the magnum's Lo-Pen multiplies that, and what remains comes off its Hits. An attack at Effect 6 or more always does at least one point (Core p.77). @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.Fi5TR1jZrgXracji]{Chat cards} gives the whole order.

Double-click the token to see the result on its track. The card keeps no record of being applied, so a second press is a second wound. That is also how one attack reaches two targets in turn.

The card's three readings, Full, Reduced and Minimum, are for creatures that take damage differently. If the selected token's traits choose one, the card marks it for you.

A Reaction

It is the creature's turn, and the Traveller dodges. A Reaction comes when she is about to be attacked, so take it before the attack is rolled (Core p.75-76).

  1. Right-click the Traveller in the tracker and choose Dodge. A card states what the attacker takes and what she will take on her own next actions.
  2. The attacker's penalty is announced and never applied. Double-click the creature's token, click Demo — Bite, and type that penalty into Custom DM.
  3. The prompt opens on the creature's Melee (natural), which the Bite is bound to. A printed animal lists its skills, and they go on the Actor as any skill does.
  4. Press Roll, then Roll damage.
  5. Select the Traveller's token and press Apply.

Her own penalty looks after itself: the next check she makes in this encounter carries a Reactions row in Modifiers, ticked like any other. It stays until you clear it. Nothing clears a Traveller's Reactions at the end of a round, so right-click her in the tracker and choose Clear reactions once she has acted. Dive for cover and Parry work the same way.

What a wound does

Her worn @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoArmorDeckVst]{Demo — Deck Vest} gives her Protection, and the Bite's AP cuts through part of it. The rest goes down her damage chain: END first, then the links after it, each to zero before the next takes anything (Core p.77). The order is stored on the Traveller, so the card never asks.

Look at her sheet. The END gauge has fallen, and the DM follows the score, so every check that reads END now reads lower. The carrying limit reads current STR and END, so a wound can also turn on Encumbrance. Unconscious and Dead are readouts of the chain: unconscious when a link past the first is empty, dead when every link is.

The broken heart on the sheet opens a raw damage dialog. It is for rulings and corrections, and it meets no armour.

End the fight

Foundry's own arrows move the turn and the round, and End Combat closes the encounter. Initiative, sides and Reactions all go with it, since none of them is stored on the Actor.

Healing is on the Health tab, in the Recovery block: first aid, surgery, medical care and a day's rest, each a button that posts a card. Nothing there advances time, so Rest 1 day is a day because you pressed it. See @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.32DXnPgHrfV65dkn]{The character sheet}.

A fight between ships is a different window. See @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.A0nyxKJrXcmaX0P8]{Space combat}. Next: @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.YVNlkmJlADkz5azu]{A first ship}.

This page transcribes a hull from its statblock, crews it, and flies it one jump. @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-actors.Actor.demoShipKestrel1]{Demo — Kestrel-class Courier} stands in for the page of the book: open it from the pack and keep it beside your work, because it is the same ship already filled in.

You also need Demo — Traveller from the last two pages, imported, and @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-actors.Actor.demoWorldBellwth]{Demo — Bellweather}, imported as well.

The hull

A spacecraft is a hull you describe with a handful of ratings. Almost everything else on the sheet derives from them.

  1. Create an Actor of type Spacecraft, and name it.
  2. Press the mode button in the title bar to go to Edit, and open the Design tab.
  3. Type what the statblock says. For the Kestrel: Hull tons 100, Configuration Streamlined, Thrust 3, Jump 2, Power plant 80, Fuel tank 22, Cargo hold 15, TL 12.

Watch the header and the rail as you go. The Hull points, drive tonnages, power rows and the budgets all fill in by themselves. A budget in red is a warning and never a refusal, since published ships break these lines.

A formula is a default, and a statblock is data. The Kestrel's yard prints 50 Hull, and the formula disagrees. Type 50 in the Hull points box of Printed figures, and the figure is marked printed wherever it appears.

Do not type a printed Hull into the Hull characteristic. On a ship it stays at 0, and anything written there is added to the derived points.

The parts list lower on the tab is optional, and none of the ratings read it. A ship with no Items at all is complete.

The crew

The roster holds stations, not people, and a station is a Crew Station Item on the ship. Four will do here.

  1. From MGT2 — Demo items, annotated, drop @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoRolePilot001]{Demo — Pilot} and @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoRoleGunner01]{Demo — Gunner} on the ship's sheet.
  2. The demo packs hold no astrogator or engineer, and a jump needs both. In the Items tab, create two Items of type Crew Station, one with Crew position Astrogator and one with Engineer, and drop them on the ship.
  3. On the Combat station tab, press the + in the Crew block once per station, and choose each row's role from its list, which is the ship's own Crew Station Items. The Station roles fold under the roster shows which ones the ship holds, and its New role button creates one on the ship directly.
  4. Drag Demo — Traveller from the Actors tab onto the Astrogator row, and again onto the Engineer row.

One person may hold two stations. A row may also be held by a typed name, as the Kestrel's are, and that is enough for a capital ship's gunners. It is not enough for a check: a check reads a skill level, so it needs a linked sheet. That is why the Kestrel as packed cannot fly the jump below. Its crew are names, and it has no astrogator's or engineer's station.

The Crew block's requirement line is advisory. Being short-handed is a legitimate state.

The mount

A mount holds the weapons and decides their damage multiple.

  1. Drop @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoWeaponTurret]{Demo — Turret Laser} on the sheet, twice.
  2. In the Mounts block, press the + that adds a mount. Choose Double Turret, label it Dorsal turret, and select both lasers in its list.
  3. On the Gunner row of the Crew block, type Dorsal turret in the Mount field.

With a linked gunner on that row, its Fire turret button makes the attack. That button knows the gunner, the mount and the linked weapons, which the bare weapon button does not. Press the mode button to return to Play. @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.IQl36fl0PKjut4bg]{Spacecraft} covers the rest of the sheet, and @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.A0nyxKJrXcmaX0P8]{Space combat} is where the mounts get used.

The leg

Open the ship's title-bar menu and choose Voyage screen. The screen flies one leg at a time.

  1. Drag Demo — Bellweather onto Here. Its profile, trade codes and zone now read from the world.
  2. In Next, type Demo — Tallow Reach. A stop may be a bare name with no document behind it.
  3. Type 2 in the parsecs box. Distance is always typed.

The line under the strip reads the leg: the fuel it burns, the Astrogation DM, the time in jump and the drive's range. A leg longer than the drive's rating turns red, and the checks can still be rolled.

Fuel

The Fuel block says this jump is short, and the Jump button is dead. A new hull's tank is empty. The Fuel tank you typed on the sheet is the tank's design size. The level aboard is a different number that starts at zero.

Type 22 in In the tank. The block now reads that the jump burns 20 tons and leaves 2: 10% of the hull per parsec of this leg (Core p.157).

That box is the only way to add fuel. There is no refuelling action, and typing a level costs nobody anything. Skimming and buying are yours to run, and the screen quotes the price per ton.

The jump

A jump is a chain of two checks (Core p.157).

  1. Press Plot. The ordinary roll prompt opens for whoever holds the Astrogator station, as an Easy (4+) check with the distance as a named DM. She holds no Astrogation, so it opens on Not proficient. Press Roll.
  2. Press Jump. The prompt opens for the Engineer station. In its Chain row, select the Plot card, because the chain is not armed for you. Press Roll.

The fuel leaves with the Jump roll, whatever the check scored. Closing the prompt instead debits nothing. Look at the tank: it reads 2.

The Engineer's Effect has now reached the Misjump block. Press Read the jump, then Post to put the outcome on the log. Under the Core procedure a clean check says so, and otherwise the block states the outcome with its dice already rolled.

That block is a readout, and nothing it finds is written to the ship. A late arrival or a damaged drive waits for you.

Arrive

Press Arrive at Demo — Tallow Reach. Next becomes Here, the first queued stop becomes Next, and the parsecs go back to 1.

That is everything the button does, and it is the only thing that moves the leg. A clean jump does not move it, and a failed one does not either. Press it when your story says they have arrived, and if a misjump put them elsewhere, set Here yourself.

What the system leaves to you

A week has passed in the story and nothing in the world knows it. The system schedules none of this, on purpose:

  • The date. Open the settings and raise the campaign day yourself.
  • Fuel. Type it, and charge for it if the crew paid.
  • The month's costs. The Finance tab works out the mortgage, maintenance, life support and salaries. Nothing bills them, and a ship has no cash balance.
  • Maintenance. Stamp the last-serviced day when the crew pays for it. The overdue flag changes no roll.
  • The stop itself. Passengers, freight and speculative goods have their own controls on @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.HZ0VLzZ4geAh88qk]{Trade}.

@UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.ZPr9rPt1v4Xq0HqD]{What this system deliberately does not do} gives the reasons. @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.LcZgrmow2Emk0b44]{Voyage and jump} covers the screen in full, including the Companion's two-Effect procedure, which each ship declares for itself on this screen.

That is the first session. Everything from here on is reference: go to the page for the screen in front of you.

This sheet is a Traveller's whole record: who they are, what has been done to them, what they carry and what they owe. It is a header, a characteristics column, six tabs and a footer, and this page takes them in that order. Creating a Traveller is a screen of its own, covered in @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.XAy8tHQw02RmRtPC]{Character creation}; this page starts from a Traveller who exists.

Every number on the sheet is one of two things. A stored number is typed, or written by a procedure, and stays until something changes it. A derived number is recomputed from the stored ones each time the Traveller is read, so it cannot be typed over and cannot go stale. The UPP, Initiative, Armor, the encumbrance cap and every characteristic's maximum are derived. Most surprises on this sheet come from reaching for a derived number and finding no field there.

Play and edit

A sheet always opens in Play. The Play / Edit button in the title bar switches it, and only someone who can edit the Traveller sees that button. The mode belongs to the open window: it is not saved, and the next opening is Play again.

Edit is for structure: the base scores, the name and title, the + on Careers and Skills, the trait chips, every gear icon, and removing a species or a Benefit. Rows offer a pencil in Edit and an eye in Play, and both open the Item; the eye opens it to be read.

Play keeps live whatever changes during a session, because a referee should not have to change modes in the middle of a fight. The states, the wound, Stun, every roll, the whole Recovery block, equipping and storing, the Finance fields and the + on the inventory blocks all work in Play. A + pressed in Play creates the Item and opens it in Edit, since a blank Item you can only read would be a dead end.

The header

The creation strip

The owner of a Traveller who has no career, no skill and no score sees Character creation not started with a Start button, which opens the creation screen with this Traveller on it. While creation runs the strip reads Character creation in progress, with the term and step reached, a Resume button and a Characteristics button that rolls the scores from the sheet. The strip goes when creation finishes. A Traveller typed in by hand loses the not started strip as soon as a score or a skill is written, and nothing is the worse for that: creation is optional, and the sheet does not depend on it.

Identity

In Play the name and a line of title, species, age and so on. In Edit those become fields.

  • Specie is free text until a species Item is linked; from then on it shows the Item's name and cannot be typed over. See Species.
  • Pronouns and Gender appear only when the world settings for them are on. They are free text and nothing reads them.
  • Sex is a different field: it appears only when the Traveller's species declares sexes, offers exactly those values, and decides which of the species' sexed modifiers apply. Every human goes without it.

States

Some of these are ticks and some are readouts, and the disabled look is the difference: you cannot untick a state the rules are imposing.

  • Encumbrance is a readout: on when the weight carried passes the cap in the footer. It goes with the encumbrance optional rule.
  • Fatigue is a tick, and yours to clear.
  • Starving is a tick, present with the starvation optional rule. Its tooltip gives this Traveller's own day counts from their END (Companion p.80), and while it is ticked Rest 1 day refuses to heal them.
  • Nausea is a tick. A radiation dose can set it, but only you can clear it, because it ends "until medical treatment received" and no number on the sheet knows when that happens (Core p.81).
  • Surgery Required is your override. Once first aid is spent and three links are still wounded, the rule imposes it and the box locks on (Core p.82).
  • Unconscious and Dead are readouts of the damage chain: unconscious when a link past the first is empty, dead when every link is (Core p.77). Passing the END check on the Recovery block overrides Unconscious until the wound grows again.

Fatigue, Nausea, Encumbrance and Starving do real work. Each stands on checks as a named row in the roll prompt, where it can be waived: Fatigue and Nausea on every check, Encumbrance and Starving on STR, DEX and END checks only. See @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.AFpVHfj7ijV7S9ct]{The roll prompt in full}.

Four states also show on the token. The Encumbered, Unconscious and Dead icons follow the sheet, and one placed by hand on the token is taken away again, because it is a readout. Fatigued runs both ways: tick it on the sheet or toggle it on the token and the other side follows. The bookkeeping needs a referee connected.

The statline

  • UPP is computed from the six characteristics' maximums, so a wound does not change it and a permanent loss does. A species that replaces one of the six prints its own characteristic in that position. It is never typed on a Traveller.
  • Initiative is the DM. Click the word to roll. The characteristic behind it is set in the Configuration dialog; DEX is the default.
  • Life is the sum of the damage chain, and clicking it opens the damage dialog. It and the track beneath it appear only when the world setting Show Life in sheet is on, and it is off by default.
  • Stun is stored, and the number is its own control: click it and type. Raising it drains END alone, and whatever END cannot absorb is reported as rounds of incapacitation (Core p.79). Lowering it gives that much END back. The eraser beside it is an hour's rest: it clears the Stun and that much of the wound with it. The wound track hatches the Stun portion so you can see which part of the damage an hour will return.
  • Armor adds worn armour, fitted augments that carry Protection and any Armour trait. Armour is worn with the shield on its row. Where worn armour has a second Protection against a damage type, hovering the figure lists what each type meets.
  • Rads is the running total, present with the radiation optional rule.

The broken heart at the end of the line opens the same damage dialog as Life. It is always there, so a table that hides Life can still wound someone.

The characteristics column

The column groups characteristics by what they do rather than by where they came from.

Damage track holds the links of the damage chain, each with a gauge; the arrows beside the heading give the order damage takes. Constants holds everything else that shows; nothing depletes here, so there is no gauge and a single number until a wound makes the two differ. Psionic reserve holds PSI, with its own amount box and Spend and Recover buttons, because PSI is outside the chain and no damage reaches it. Its group appears only when the psionics optional rule is on, which it is not by default, and the Traveller has Show Psionic Talents ticked in Configuration.

Click a characteristic's name or its DM to roll it. In Edit each row becomes one input for base, with the modifier and the resulting maximum beside it.

Worn armour that raises STR or DEX, such as battle dress, prints the raised score as a small boxed number beside the Traveller's own, and the DM is the boxed number's. Checks, melee damage, Initiative and the carrying limit read it; damage still drains the Traveller's own score and gauge (Core p.102). Hover the box to see which armour raised it.

Base is the score as first rolled, and nothing should ever rewrite it. Everything that moves a score later lands beside it: a species modifier, a fitted augment, the radiation penalty on END and each row of Permanent changes go to auto, and Active Effects go to effect. The maximum is base plus both. If a score looks wrong, the gear on its row shows the split. Do not correct the base to match; find the row that moved it.

The gear opens a small dialog with the two stored numbers, Base and Damage. This is the one place damage is set outright rather than applied as an amount, which is what correcting a mistake takes. It also holds the characteristic's rank in the chain and a Show tick. A characteristic with no score cannot enter the chain, since there would be nothing to drain.

Beyond the six and PSI, the system knows six more characteristics (morale, luck, sanity, charm, other and reputation). None of them shows unless the world has adopted it in the extraCharacteristics optional rule, and Show on a single Traveller cannot override that. A species that rolls one of those slots prints its own name and abbreviation in place of the generic one.

The damage chain

Damage drains an ordered list of characteristics, each link to zero before the next takes anything, and the last link takes whatever remains (Core p.77). A Traveller starts on END, STR, DEX. The order is stored on the Traveller, so it can be changed in the Configuration dialog: drag the rows, remove a link, or add any characteristic that has a score.

Life and the unconscious and dead states all read this list. An empty chain means no damage lands at all, with no error.

The damage dialog

The Life figure, the wound track and the broken heart all open it. You type an Amount and choose Damage or Heal, and a map shows where the points will land before anything is written. The states the hit would cause light up beneath it. Nothing changes until Apply.

When damage passes the first link and more than one link could take the rest, Overflow falls on appears: Core p.77 gives the target that choice, so it is asked here each time rather than assumed from the chain's order.

This dialog is raw. A number typed here names no weapon, so it meets no armour, no scale and no Effect floor. An attack goes through the damage card instead, which applies all of those; see @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.Fi5TR1jZrgXracji]{Chat cards}.

Heal here is a flat undo that walks the chain backwards, repairing the link injured last. The rulebook's procedures are on the Recovery block and divide their points as the book says.

Health

This tab is everything that has happened to the Traveller's body. All of it works in Play.

Radiation

Headed Health, and present with the radiation optional rule. Rads is the count, and it is a field because anti-rad drugs lower it and nothing else does (Core p.81). Beside it are the standing END penalty read from that count, and the Rad score of worn armour.

Expose takes a dose: choose a source to roll one or type a number. Armour's Rad score comes off it, the immediate effects land at once, and the new running total can cost END. That END penalty is derived from the count, so lowering Rads gives it back. With the rule off the block goes and the stored count waits, untouched, in case the rule comes back.

Recovery

The rulebook's healing procedures as buttons (Core p.82-83). The readouts above them say how many chain links are wounded, the END DM, whether first aid is spent, and the highest implant Tech Level, which is what a facility has to answer to.

Nothing here advances time. Rest 1 day is a day because you pressed it, and the system keeps no clock that could press it for you. Each button posts a card to chat saying what it did.

  • First aid opens a pool of points to place across the wounded links as you like. From the sheet it opens at the minimum of 1, because the sheet has no check to read an Effect from; change the figure, or roll the Medic check and use the first-aid button on its card, which brings the Effect with it. It can be used once. When a new injury means it is available again, the reset arrow beside the buttons clears it.
  • Surgery asks for the Effect and works out the points, which you may overrule. A success opens the same pool. A failure costs the patient points through the chain, where the unconscious threshold and death are waiting. The button lights up when surgery is needed.
  • Medical care asks for the doctor's Medic level and spreads its points evenly by itself. It lights up when one or two links are wounded after first aid.
  • Rest 1 day rolls the formula printed on the button. While surgery is required the formula is the END DM alone, so a negative DM makes the patient worse.
  • Mental 1 day returns a point each to wounded INT and EDU. They are not in the chain, so no other button reaches them.
  • PSI rest asks how many hours passed and returns the reserve at the book's rate (Core p.228). It appears with psionics.
  • END check rolls to wake an unconscious Traveller, and each failure adds to the next attempt. The DM on the button is the one the next roll will use. A pass wakes them without healing them.

Wounds

A wound here is a disease Item of the wound sub-type: a lasting injury written down as a document, with a difficulty for treating it. It is not the damage on the chain, which needs no Item. The list is for injuries worth naming, like @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-items.Item.demoWoundShoulde]{Demo — Torn Shoulder}. Its + is Edit-only.

Permanent changes

One signed log for everything that moves a score for good: ageing, injuries from creation, events, the medical care that undoes them, and characteristics bought with training. Each row adds to the characteristic's auto, so base still holds the score as rolled, and the readout above the table prints what each moved characteristic stands at against that.

The + records a row by hand. It takes a source, an optional term, age and roll, a signed change per characteristic, a cost and a note. Tick Bill it and the cost comes out of Cash On Hand, with whatever cannot be paid going to Debt, and the Finance notes name the source. Rows are added and removed, never edited, and removing one simply takes it out of the sum, so the score moves back.

Stored valueMeaning
ageingAgeing
injuryInjury
eventEvent
medicalCareMedical care
ageingCrisisCareAgeing crisis care
refereeReferee
trainingTraining

Two warnings can appear here, and they are different facts. An ageing crisis: a characteristic stands at 0 is the moment a doctor can still do something, and the source ageing crisis care rolls its own price. This Traveller has survived an ageing crisis is permanent and stays after the care, because the row that took the score to 0 is still in the log: Core p.49 has them fail every later qualification roll, and a change of assignment that asks for one. @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.demo-actors.Actor.demoCharHesperLd]{Demo — Hesper Lund} shows the second.

PSI raises neither warning. Aged to 0 it is no crisis, and care does not restore it: the Traveller has lost their psionic abilities for good (Aliens of Charted Space 1 p.275). See Psionic Talents.

Diseases

Diseases and poisons, both disease Items. Clicking the name opens the roll prompt on END with the Item's difficulty, and the Item's damage formula rides the card. The interval on the row is a sentence for you to read; nothing fires when it passes.

Traits & Skills

Species

A Traveller's species is one embedded species Item, and the sheet keeps a pointer to it and copies nothing. Everything this block shows is read live from the Item: its description, modifiers and traits. Change the Item and the Traveller changes.

Drop a species Item on the sheet, or follow the link in the empty block to open the @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.BF6kF7dg9C8NiEY3]{compendium explorer} on species. Dropping one links it and shows any characteristic slots it rolls. A second species is refused with a message, unless the speciesModifiersStack optional rule allows sub-variants to add to a parent. The trash, in Edit, removes the Item and breaks the link. Species modifiers apply to auto and never to base, so removing a species removes its modifiers cleanly.

A table with no species Items can type a name in the identity block. That text does nothing mechanical.

Traits

The Traveller's own trait chips, typed in Edit. The list suggests names from the trait registry, and a trait's parameters can be retyped on the chip. The species' traits appear on the Species block and are not editable here, but they count all the same. The registry holds names and parameters, not rules text: the book says what a trait means, and the system reads those few it has a rule for.

Careers

One row per career, with terms and rank, each a career Item. Creation writes these; for a Traveller finished on paper, drop a career Item or use the Edit-only +. A shared table Item is refused here, since it is not a career, and during creation a second career cannot be dropped over one still being served.

Skills and training

A skill is a talent Item embedded on the Traveller, and everything that reads a skill matches it by name. Click the name to roll it. There is no list of skills on the Actor to edit: to give someone a skill, drop one or use the Edit-only +, which is why a blank Traveller has no skills at all.

The strip above the table shows each open training programme and at most one action. With nothing open it offers Start training…. The training window is where a programme is opened, read and closed.

Two engines can run here, chosen by the advancementSystem optional rule, and each programme remembers which it was started under:

  • Core (Core p.55) shows eight boxes for the weeks of a Study Period and pips for periods passed, failed and still needed. Eight boxes rather than a number because the weeks need not be consecutive. The button logs a week, offers the check once the period is complete, and offers the level when enough periods have passed.
  • Companion (Companion p.41) shows a bar of Experience Points against the price of the next level.

Two things cannot be trained, and the row says why with an info icon rather than offering a button: Jack-of-all-Trades (Core p.55), and under the Companion's table SOC and PSI. In Edit, a small hatch beneath the strip exposes the top programme's stored target, weeks and characteristic for repairs. Athletics can be learned against any physical characteristic (Core p.55), which is what that characteristic field is for.

Psionic Talents

Talents are talent Items of the psionic sub-type. The block appears when the psionics optional rule is on and the Traveller's Configuration has Show Psionic Talents ticked. Clicking one rolls it with the reach and PSI cost on the prompt, and a Traveller with no PSI left is refused. A Traveller who lost PSI to ageing is refused for good, and their psionic skills leave the prompt's skill list too.

Inventory

Three sub-tabs, and everything in them is an embedded Item. The Traveller accepts armour, weapons, ammunition, computers, containers, equipment, drugs and general items into the inventory, and contacts, diseases, careers, talents and species into their own blocks. Other Item types are refused without comment.

On Hand

What the Traveller is carrying, by type: Weapons, Armors, Augments, Computers, Softwares, Equipments, Items. Ammunition, drugs and containers carried on the body list under Items. Each name that rolls opens the roll prompt, and for a weapon that is an attack: see @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.AFpVHfj7ijV7S9ct]{The roll prompt in full}.

Each row's controls:

  • The shield equips or unequips. It appears only where the Item type has such a state. Armour protects only while worn. An augment improves nobody until fitted, and the same shield fits it. An Item's Active Effects reach the Traveller only while it is equipped, and an Item dropped on the sheet arrives unequipped.
  • The bolt appears on powered armour and switches the suit off when its power runs out, and on again. A suit switched off weighs a quarter of its mass, loses its bonuses and doubles its penalties (CSC p.35).
  • The inbox stores the Item in a container. It goes to the one chosen under Drop In on Storage, or the first the Traveller has, or a new one created for the purpose. On a carried container the same button puts it down, and its weight stops counting.
  • The eye or pencil opens the Item, and the trash deletes it.

Carried weight is counted in the footer. Worn armour counts for a quarter of its weight, and powered armour for nothing while it is switched on.

Software runs on a host. Drag a software Item onto a computer's row, onto worn armour with a Processing rating, onto a fitted augment or onto equipment that carries one, and it nests under the host. A host prints Bandwidth used against Processing. Three icons warn: too much Bandwidth for the host, more than one package on a Processing 0 host, and a package the host's Tech Level cannot run. All three are advisory: the package stays loaded and marked, because the rules say what happens and the referee rules on it. The eject button takes one out. Loose software waits in the Softwares list.

A second skill augmentation gets a warning under the Augments table (Core p.107), and stays fitted.

Storage

Containers and what is in them. The picker filters the list by container and also offers (all); Drop In sets where stored Items go. New Items made from this tab go straight into the container.

Dragging an Item onto a container row moves it in. A container cannot end up inside itself. The two ways to delete a container differ: the trash beside the picker puts its contents back on hand first, while the trash on a carried container's row in Items deletes everything inside it. A locked container hides its contents from players on this sheet and refuses their drops, but its total weight still prints; a lock withholds what is inside, not how much the case weighs. Locking here is a courtesy between friends. A real secret belongs in a @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.T98Xoe71SmJYvNvx]{stash}.

Finance

Cash On Hand is the Traveller's money, and it is what mustering out banks into and what a medical bill is paid from. Pension, Living Cost, Debt, Ship Shares, Ship payment and the notes are stored figures. Nothing bills them on a schedule: the system keeps no clock.

Ship payment is what this Traveller pays towards a hull the crew owns together, typed, because the book bills the crew and leaves the split to the table (Core p.154). Ship Shares are earned before any ship exists and come off a ship's price (Core p.149).

The transfer icon gives this Traveller's money to someone else. Taking another Traveller's money is the referee's screen, reached from the token controls.

With the wealth optional rule on, a Wealth (WLT) line reads a score and DM off Cash On Hand (Companion p.4). It is a readout, and the ledger stays the truth.

Benefits is a ledger of what careers owed. A Benefit such as "any armour up to a given price and Tech Level" is a right with limits, not an object, so a row records the right and the player redeems it against the referee's library with the hand icon. A redeemed row stays, so the sheet can show what paid for what. The + records one for a Traveller who finished on paper, and spends no Benefit roll.

Contacts

Allies, Contacts, Rivals, Enemies and Patrons, each a contact Item with relation, attitude, occupation and location. Creation adds them from event rows, often with the name New Contact for you to fill in.

Biography

Two rich-text fields, Biography and Notes, each with its own edit toggle. They do not depend on the sheet's mode.

Effects

Every Active Effect that can reach this Traveller, including those carried by owned Items. An effect on gear that is not equipped lists as inactive, and works again once the gear is. Each row can be switched off, suspended, edited or deleted, and a dose that is running can be ended. The changes column prints each one's key, value and phase. See @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.8jfYJ4JuROi9vd17]{Active Effects}, which explains why a drug on the shelf does nothing until it is taken.

The footer

The gauge is the carried weight against the encumbrance cap: STR plus END at their current values, plus the levels of any skill whose Item has Reduce Encumbrance ticked (Core p.98). Because the cap reads current values, a wound can put someone over it. Over the cap, the flag appears and the Encumbrance state turns on. With the encumbrance optional rule off, the gauge gives way to a plain total.

The gear in Edit opens Configuration, which holds three things:

  • Show Psionic Talents, offered only when the world has adopted psionics.
  • Initiative: the characteristic it reads, or none and a Flat DM in its place.
  • Damage Order: the damage chain.

The gear beside the Damage track heading opens the same dialog.

One Actor type covers both a person and an animal, because the rules hurt them the same way: damage drains a chain, and a creature's chain happens to have one link. What separates them is a Preset, and it decides the blocks the sheet draws, the damage chain, the characteristics shown and whether the token is linked.

The sheet is one column of blocks with no tabs. Play and Edit, rolling, the damage dialog, the Stun number and the trait chips all work as on the @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.32DXnPgHrfV65dkn]{character sheet}.

In Edit, the Creature preset's statline has a Hits field beside the readout: type the score there, and the size band and the four states follow.

A person

The header carries Role, Specie, Attitude and Experience in Edit, and prints them in Play.

UPP is a typed field here, where on a Traveller it is computed. A referee transcribing an NPC has the printed code and may never fill in the six characteristics, so whatever you type prints as it stands; left blank, it derives from the six. Typing it changes no score and no DM: a check still reads the characteristics themselves.

Experience and Combatant together name a row of the Core's Experience ladder (Core p.92). The ladder's suggested skill level shows in the tooltip, and that is all the two fields do. It is a hint beside the field and generates nothing.

Attitude is a label. Nothing rolls on it.

A person has Fatigue, Unconscious and Dead, read as on a Traveller, and the Life figure if the world setting shows it. With the radiation optional rule on, either preset also shows Nausea, and Rads on the statline: the number opens the exposure control, as on a Traveller, and a creature takes the dose's immediate damage on its Hits with no END to lose. A person has no recovery block, no finance and no careers: an NPC is a statblock rather than a life. A wound is healed with the Heal direction of the damage dialog.

A creature

The header

Diet and Pattern are independent. The published statblocks pair them freely, so the sheet treats diet as flavour and reads the reaction from the pattern alone (Core p.89-90).

Group is two numbers, how many are present and how many there were, and only a referee can change them. Printed statblocks give no number appearing, so one Actor can stand for a pack on a single sheet. The count is a stored tally and a token bar can show it. No roll or damage reads it, so killing one is yours to count down.

Hits is the lead figure and opens the damage dialog. Size is the DM ranged attacks gain against this animal, read from the Large or Small trait (Core p.85). It is printed for the attacker to add; no prompt reads it.

The track beneath runs to twice the starting Hits, because the wound is stored and can pass the maximum, and it carries four marks:

  • Driven off at half the starting Hits gone. This is the referee's option in the book (Core p.85), so the sheet reports it and acts on nothing.
  • Unconscious at nine tenths gone.
  • Dead at all of them gone.
  • Destroyed at twice the starting Hits, where the body is no use to anyone.

Incapacitated is a fifth state: Stun damage has reached half the starting Hits (Core p.84). Stun on a creature is tracked on Hits, where a Traveller's comes off END, and the eraser clears it the same way.

Behaviour

With a pattern chosen, the block prints the thresholds and Roll 2D posts a reaction card saying whether it flees, attacks or carries on (Core p.90). Some patterns hang on something only you can see, such as who surprised whom or who is larger. The sheet prints that question beneath the figures, and the card repeats it, because it has no way to answer it.

Speed

Ground and Swim are metres per Minor Action (Core p.84). Fly is a Speed Band, not a distance, because that is what the Flyer trait names. Note takes any movement the statblock prints without a figure.

Attacks

A creature's attack is an ordinary weapon Item with Natural ticked, so it rolls, reports its Effect and applies damage exactly as a pistol does. The + makes an ordinary weapon, which lands in the Weapons block until you open it and tick Natural. Only then does it move to Attacks.

A creature has no STR, so its melee attacks add none. The damage on the Item is the whole figure; the Animal Size table sets it (Core p.89).

The last readouts

Below the traits, four readings of the trait list:

  • Damage response is how this creature's traits make it take an attack, and the damage card uses it.
  • Scale is ground, or spacecraft for a Gigantic creature, and that also applies to damage.
  • Conditional armour is the Armour trait's second score, such as +6 vs. fire. The damage card adds it to the first against the damage types it names. Hover it to see which; one that names none, such as psionics, is added by nothing.
  • Suggested size is the Animal Size row these Hits fall in, for comparison only. The published statblocks break that table constantly, and the sheet does not mind.

Blocks both presets share

Attacks and Weapons split weapons on the Natural flag. A person's sidearm belongs in Weapons, and it is dropped on the sheet like anything else.

Skills works as on a Traveller, including the + being Edit-only. A creature's block notes the book's default skills, which the sheet does not add for you.

Traits are chips, in the animal vocabulary for a creature and the species vocabulary for a person. Traits do work here: Armour feeds the Armor figure, Fast Metabolism and Slow Metabolism move Initiative, Large and Small move Size, and Gigantic changes the scale.

Specie is for a person only. It behaves as on a Traveller, and it can be left empty.

Biography and Notes are rich text.

Give an NPC its Protection with the Armour trait, which is how a statblock prints it. An armour Item dropped here gets a row of its own under Armors, with the shield to wear it, the eye to open it and the trash to delete it. Worn, its Protection adds to the trait's. A second score the Item carries replaces its own Protection against the damage types it names, where the trait's second score adds to the first.

The gear beside the broken heart in Edit opens Configuration, for the damage chain and Initiative. A creature has no footer and no characteristics column, so this is the only way in. A creature with Fast Metabolism needs no Flat DM as well: the trait is added on top of it.

A vehicle is a transcribed statblock with a Hull pool, armour on six faces and a critical track. Nothing about its design is computed from parts: what the book prints is what the sheet holds. Where a figure can be checked against the design rules, the sheet shows the disagreement and never corrects it.

A vehicle's token is unlinked, because several of the same model go on the map and each takes its own damage.

Transcribing a statblock

In Edit, the header takes the printed lines: TL, Spaces, Hull, Crew, Passengers, Cargo, Shipping, Cost and Range with its unit. The readout grid above them is the same data as the book prints it.

Hull is typed here, and this is the reverse of a spacecraft, whose Hull derives from its tonnage. See @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.IQl36fl0PKjut4bg]{Spacecraft}.

Speed is stored as a band and shown by name, because collision damage and several DMs count bands. Cruise has its own selector, since the book's figure need not be one band under maximum.

Agility is typed in its own block: the printed figure for the vehicle's native medium, signed.

The Chassis block holds the skill and speciality it takes to operate the vehicle. A multi-mode vehicle has more than one pair. The chassis also tells the sheet which medium is native.

Hull

The bar fills as the hull takes damage, and Wrecked is the only state beyond it (Core p.140). The hint beneath counts how many tenths of the Hull have been passed. Each is a Severity 1 critical in the book, and the count is there to tell you one is owed: a wound never raises a critical by itself, on this sheet or from a card. You roll the location and apply it on the Criticals block.

Clicking the Hull figure, or the broken heart, opens the damage dialog, with Repair in place of Heal. That dialog is raw: it meets no armour and picks no facing. An attack goes through the damage card, where a facing strip appears for a vehicle. See @UUID[Compendium.mgt2.guide.JournalEntry.3wd9e5Iz4A9besSS.JournalEntryPage.Fi5TR1jZrgXracji]{Chat cards}.

Agility, in play

Printed is what you transcribed; Effective is what the vehicle has now, and the penalties that explain the difference are listed as chips.

Operating mode and Towing stay live in Play, because they change during a session. A mode the chassis is not built for costs Agility. A vehicle tows while it is doing something else, so towing is a separate tick.

Terrain counts only under the Handbook's rules. It lands on the check, on Agility and on both Speed Bands at once, and some terrain is impassable to a chassis; the block then says so. The ATV, Off-Roader and Tracked traits decide which column applies, and Smart Wheels improves it by one (VH2026 p.20).

Under the Handbook's rules the block also prints the turn rate, the rounds for a half turn, the delay that negative Agility adds to a task, and the G-force of a turn against the vehicle's limit. G-force is an optional rule in the book, so the sheet prints it and does nothing with it (VH2026 p.19-20).

Environment

Drawn under the Handbook's rules, and it matters for any aircraft that is not grav. The world it was built for is transcription; the world it is over now is yours to set, and stays live in Play. State all four digits and the sheet reads the step between them: a DM, a shift in Speed Band, a share of Range, and whether the aircraft can fly here at all (VH2026 p.20-22). Leave any one blank and nothing is assumed. These digits are typed; the sheet does not read them from a world Actor.

Combat actions

Dogfighting and evasive action are the driver's skill checks with the vehicle's Agility as a DM (Core p.138), so the seat has to be filled first. Drop a Traveller or an NPC on the sheet and they are the driver; the buttons refuse otherwise. Dropping another person replaces them. The name in the block opens their sheet.

The roll prompt opens on the driver's own skills, preselecting the chassis skill if they have it. Agility arrives as a row you can waive, as does the Control DM from any critical. Under the Handbook's rules, the part of a negative Agility that a round of Minor Actions can cancel is a row of its own, and unticking it is what spending them looks like.

  • Dogfight is an opposed check. Set the opposition on the prompt, or nothing is stored. It stores the winner's or loser's DM, and the winner's margin carries into the next round's check.
  • Evasive stores the Effect, which stands as a negative DM on attacks made from this vehicle. The same Effect counts against attacks aimed at the vehicle (Core p.138), and those attackers apply it themselves, since their roll is not this sheet's.

Both DMs then stand as rows on any attack made from the vehicle. They last until you clear them, with the arrow in the block heading, because nothing on the sheet can watch a round go by.

Speed

The two band selectors stay live, since a driver's speed changes during a fight. If criticals, terrain or the environment push the band in play below the printed maximum, an Effective line appears. Under the Handbook's rules the block adds rounds to reach the band, distance per round and km/h at the band in play.

Armour

Six faces, each with its own number (VH2026 p.55). The damage card takes the facing the attack came from, and with none named the front answers.

Dorsal and Ventral may be left blank, and blank is different from 0. A blank face answers with half the port armour for the roof and half the aft for the floor (Core p.140), and its cell says so. A 0 is a statement that the roof has no armour, and it overrides that. Clearing the field restores the fallback.

Reactive armour is a second number per face, typed in Edit and added to that face. You reduce it by hand as it is spent.

The readouts beneath give the extra armour against light weapons, which equals the TL, the to-hit DM a target this size gives attackers, and monthly maintenance at half a per cent of Cost (VH2026 p.5). The to-hit figure is printed for the attacker to add; no prompt reads it.

Systems

Six lines, each its own kind of number, and the Applies to column says whose roll each one touches. A blank is different from 0: a printed dash means the vehicle lacks the system, and Sensors genuinely prints +0 on some vehicles. Camouflage and Stealth are DMs on the observer's roll, so they are zero or negative: type a positive number and it is clamped to 0. They are printed for you to apply.

Add a mount with its +, then give it weapons in the multi-select. A weapon on no mount is listed beneath, marked on no mount, and it still rolls.
